person: Beverly Shaw is a 72-year-old retired fourth-grade teacher in Roanoke, Virginia. She is married to Harold, 74, who works part-time at a hardware store, and she does paid substitute and tutoring work. They are raising their grandchildren Lena, 9, and Mateo, 13, and Camille, 22, lives with them while she attends community college full time. Their 2023 earned income credit was disallowed in an audit, and the 2025 return is on extension. She is nervous about the whole thing after losing $800 to a scam last spring, and she wants every step explained before it happens. Her daughter phones on Sundays and asks whether she has dealt with the bank yet.
stated_up_front: Hello, I'm sorry, I'm not very good with these things. My grandson said you could help me finish our tax return that's on extension, the one with the children's credit. Could you please tell me what you're going to do before you do it?

facts.truth: Beverly and Harold Shaw file jointly; the 2025 return has been on extension since the extension was accepted on 14 April 2026.
Granddaughter, 9, has lived with them all of 2025 and is in fourth grade.
Grandson, 13, came to live with them in early March 2025. She remembers 'about five months' but thinks the school record gives the exact date.
Granddaughter, 22, lives at home and is a full-time student at Virginia Western Community College.
The IRS disallowed their 2023 earned income credit after an audit letter. She kept the letter, and it was not a simple math mistake.
Harold's W-2 from Blue Ridge Hardware shows about $19,400 in wages.
Beverly's W-2 from Roanoke County Schools for substitute teaching shows about $11,800.
Dorian, a grandson, stayed with them about four months in 2025 and then went back to his mother, who sent a signed Form 8332 in the mail.
Jonas, 21, is another grandson who lives with them and works full time at a warehouse. He is not in school.
Priya is a niece who lives in the house with her mother, Harold's sister, and her mother says she is claiming her.
Two emails arrived, one offering a quick refund advance with a $99 fee and one from a 'credit maximizer' that wants the children's names for 20 percent. She distrusts both.

unknowns: What Form 8862 is and whether it must go with this return
Whether a Form 8332 from a child's mother can move the earned income credit
Who wins when a niece's own mother also wants to claim her
The exact date on Mateo's school record showing when he moved in
